issues.body:
<!-- makarba-catalog-id:00.01 -->
### Summary
Branch/PR rules, ownership vacancies and planning-only boundary are documented.

### Why this is needed
Establish repository governance enables the requirements, research and repository foundation workstream while preserving the researcher-led evidence chain. Without this deliverable: no real team or source licence invented is not established or verified.

### User story
As a project contributor, I need this reviewed capability so that branch/PR rules, ownership vacancies and planning-only boundary are documented.

### Scope
- Branch/PR rules, ownership vacancies and planning-only boundary are documented.
- Implement/review the associated contract and observable error states described in `docs/product/requirements.md`.
- Capture evidence for the negative case: No real team or source licence invented.

### Out of scope
Other backlog issue deliverables, unrelated refactors, real data committed to Git, and unapproved paid-provider activation. Planning/design/research issues produce reviewed artifacts rather than application code; implementation issues build only the stated capability.

### Technical approach
Review AGENTS, contribution/security policy and licence decision register. Follow `docs/product/requirements.md`, `docs/architecture/data-model.md` and the relevant ADR. Keep migrations, runtime validation and UI contracts consistent where this task changes them. Document a justified alternative before changing architecture.

### Data and privacy considerations
Documentation contains no credentials, real participant records, invented approvals or exact interview coordinates. Do not copy sensitive inputs into issue comments, test artifacts or operational logs.

### Dependencies
Hard prerequisites for starting implementation: None.

Live integration prerequisites (prepare with synthetic mocks; do not claim production integration until verified): None.

Soft review inputs: None.

Operational/real-data gates: None. Institutional consent, verified geography, rights and privacy requirements remain mandatory.

Rationale: Original prerequisites retained; no contract-first relaxation needed.

See `docs/project/implementation-order.md` for readiness and completion semantics.

### Implementation steps
1. Read linked design, verify blocker evidence and identify the exact files/contracts affected.
2. Review AGENTS, contribution/security policy and licence decision register.
3. Cover the positive contract “Branch/PR rules, ownership vacancies and planning-only boundary are documented” and failure condition “No real team or source licence invented”.
4. Update the linked documentation and record verification commands/results or reviewed research evidence in the PR.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Branch/PR rules, ownership vacancies and planning-only boundary are documented.
- [ ] No real team or source licence invented.
- [ ] The PR includes a reproducible demonstration or independently reviewable artifact proving the stated contract, with no real participant data.
- [ ] Associated permissions, lifecycle/error states and source limitations are documented in `docs/product/requirements.md`.

### Required tests
- Positive contract: demonstrate branch/PR rules, ownership vacancies and planning-only boundary are documented using an explicit fixture/checklist and expected outcome.
- Negative/edge contract: verify “No real team or source licence invented” with a failing-path fixture or documented independent review.
- Document review: check source citations, traceability and concrete acceptance evidence; no mirror-of-document unit tests.
- Privacy check: Documentation contains no credentials, real participant records, invented approvals or exact interview coordinates.

### Edge cases
No real team or source licence invented. Also inspect absent/retired source data, unauthorized access where applicable, interrupted operation, and stale revision rather than substituting fabricated values or silently dropping work.

### Documentation
Update `docs/product/requirements.md` and any affected requirements/ADR/test case. Record verification evidence, unresolved external dependency and compatibility/rollback impact in the implementation report.

### Definition of Done
All acceptance boxes have evidence; relevant tests/reviews pass; changes stay within scope; security/privacy and source accuracy are reviewed; documentation is current; PR/commit and CI results are linked. Compilation alone is insufficient. Follow `docs/project/definition-of-done.md`.

### Priority
P0 — release/privacy/foundation blocker.

### Size
S — 1 effort points. Review AGENTS, contribution/security policy and licence decision register; includes scoped implementation/review, negative tests and integration evidence (S, 1 points).

### Labels
area:devops, handoff:required, owner:developer-a, phase:foundation, priority:p0, size:s, status:ready, type:docs, workstream:core-platform.

### Milestone
M00 — Requirements, Research and Repository Foundation

<!-- two-developer-allocation:start -->
### Two-developer ownership and execution plan

Primary owner: **Developer A — `satvikp-coder`**. Exactly one implementation owner; the other developer reviews/supports the boundary.

Actual GitHub assignment: assigned to satvikp-coder; verified by GitHub issue API. Developer B assignees are intentionally unchanged while the invitation remains unaccepted, per owner instruction; ownership labels reserve the work.

Workstream: `core-platform`. Phase: `foundation`. Owner order: **A-01**; global topological reference 1 (not a lockstep schedule). Suggested start wave: Sprint 0; no calendar deadline. Ready to start technically: **yes**.

Expected deliverable: Branch/PR rules, ownership vacancies and planning-only boundary are documented.

Estimate: S / 1 points, considering implementation, uncertainty, test burden and integration. Re-estimate after the first vertical slices; waiting for an external institution is not counted as engineering effort.

Required contracts: baseline; see `docs/project/developer-handoffs.md`. Integration partner: B (varunkarthic), pending collaboration acceptance.

Handoff requirement: Publish versioned DTO/schema/fixtures and conformance evidence; review cross-stream providers ; consumers #2.

Review requirement: Cross-review public/private interface, schema or grants before integration; never grant unrestricted raw access for UI/reporting work. Original acceptance criteria, required tests, PR references and research requirements are preserved. Hard prerequisites must be evidenced. Mock-backed local components may be accepted with conformance tests; listed live integrations must pass their named gates before production claims. Integration issues require their runtime integration dependencies before final acceptance.

Documentation: update the relevant original architecture/design documents plus the generated allocation record when dependencies, estimates or acceptance evidence change. Use `dev-a/issue-1-short-description`, an up-to-date main, scoped PR, relevant tests and CI. No feature implementation is included in this allocation run.

<!-- two-developer-allocation:end -->

<!-- makarba-catalog-id:12.09 -->
### Summary
Only approved deidentified input can produce reviewed labeled draft themes.

### Why this is needed
Evaluate human-reviewed qualitative AI assistance enables the advanced and stretch features workstream while preserving the researcher-led evidence chain. Without this deliverable: no raw interviews sent to external model or unsourced summaries auto-published is not established or verified.

### User story
As a public research reader, I need this reviewed capability so that only approved deidentified input can produce reviewed labeled draft themes.

### Scope
- Only approved deidentified input can produce reviewed labeled draft themes.
- Implement/review the associated contract and observable error states described in `docs/project/release-plan.md`.
- Capture evidence for the negative case: No raw interviews sent to external model or unsourced summaries auto-published.

### Out of scope
Other backlog issue deliverables, unrelated refactors, real data committed to Git, and unapproved paid-provider activation. Planning/design/research issues produce reviewed artifacts rather than application code; implementation issues build only the stated capability.

### Technical approach
Privacy/model/vendor approval, human coding comparison and provenance. Follow `docs/project/release-plan.md`, `docs/architecture/data-model.md` and the relevant ADR. Keep migrations, runtime validation and UI contracts consistent where this task changes them. Document a justified alternative before changing architecture.

### Data and privacy considerations
Stretch features cannot weaken core privacy, evidence, accessibility or rights controls. Do not copy sensitive inputs into issue comments, test artifacts or operational logs.

### Dependencies
Hard prerequisites for starting implementation: #86 (08.03); #105 (09.10); #126 (11.09).

Live integration prerequisites (prepare with synthetic mocks; do not claim production integration until verified): None.

Soft review inputs: None.

Operational/real-data gates: None. Institutional consent, verified geography, rights and privacy requirements remain mandatory.

Rationale: Original prerequisites retained; no contract-first relaxation needed.

See `docs/project/implementation-order.md` for readiness and completion semantics.

### Implementation steps
1. Read linked design, verify blocker evidence and identify the exact files/contracts affected.
2. Privacy/model/vendor approval, human coding comparison and provenance.
3. Cover the positive contract “Only approved deidentified input can produce reviewed labeled draft themes” and failure condition “No raw interviews sent to external model or unsourced summaries auto-published”.
4. Update the linked documentation and record verification commands/results or reviewed research evidence in the PR.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Only approved deidentified input can produce reviewed labeled draft themes.
- [ ] No raw interviews sent to external model or unsourced summaries auto-published.
- [ ] The PR includes a reproducible demonstration or independently reviewable artifact proving the stated contract, with no real participant data.
- [ ] Associated permissions, lifecycle/error states and source limitations are documented in `docs/project/release-plan.md`.

### Required tests
- Positive contract: demonstrate only approved deidentified input can produce reviewed labeled draft themes using an explicit fixture/checklist and expected outcome.
- Negative/edge contract: verify “No raw interviews sent to external model or unsourced summaries auto-published” with a failing-path fixture or documented independent review.
- Run relevant domain unit checks and API/database/browser or real-device checks for the components changed; record exact commands, fixtures and expected versus actual results.
- Privacy check: Stretch features cannot weaken core privacy, evidence, accessibility or rights controls.

### Edge cases
No raw interviews sent to external model or unsourced summaries auto-published. Also inspect absent/retired source data, unauthorized access where applicable, interrupted operation, and stale revision rather than substituting fabricated values or silently dropping work.

### Documentation
Update `docs/project/release-plan.md` and any affected requirements/ADR/test case. Record verification evidence, unresolved external dependency and compatibility/rollback impact in the implementation report.

### Definition of Done
All acceptance boxes have evidence; relevant tests/reviews pass; changes stay within scope; security/privacy and source accuracy are reviewed; documentation is current; PR/commit and CI results are linked. Compilation alone is insufficient. Follow `docs/project/definition-of-done.md`.

### Priority
P3 — optional after core release.

### Size
XL — 8 effort points. Privacy/model/vendor approval, human coding comparison and provenance; includes scoped implementation/review, negative tests and integration evidence (XL, 8 points).

### Labels
area:frontend, dependency:blocked, handoff:required, owner:developer-a, phase:parallel, priority:p3, size:xl, status:blocked, stretch-goal, type:feature, workstream:core-platform.

### Milestone
M12 — Advanced and Stretch Features

<!-- two-developer-allocation:start -->
### Two-developer ownership and execution plan

Primary owner: **Developer A — `satvikp-coder`**. Exactly one implementation owner; the other developer reviews/supports the boundary.

Actual GitHub assignment: assigned to satvikp-coder; verified by GitHub issue API. Developer B assignees are intentionally unchanged while the invitation remains unaccepted, per owner instruction; ownership labels reserve the work.

Workstream: `core-platform`. Phase: `parallel`. Owner order: **A-63**; global topological reference 135 (not a lockstep schedule). Suggested start wave: Sprint 6; no calendar deadline. Ready to start technically: **no: unresolved hard prerequisites**.

Expected deliverable: Only approved deidentified input can produce reviewed labeled draft themes.

Estimate: XL / 8 points, considering implementation, uncertainty, test burden and integration. Re-estimate after the first vertical slices; waiting for an external institution is not counted as engineering effort.

Required contracts: baseline; see `docs/project/developer-handoffs.md`. Integration partner: B (varunkarthic), pending collaboration acceptance.

Handoff requirement: Publish versioned DTO/schema/fixtures and conformance evidence; review cross-stream providers #86, #126; consumers .

Review requirement: Cross-review public/private interface, schema or grants before integration; never grant unrestricted raw access for UI/reporting work. Original acceptance criteria, required tests, PR references and research requirements are preserved. Hard prerequisites must be evidenced. Mock-backed local components may be accepted with conformance tests; listed live integrations must pass their named gates before production claims. Integration issues require their runtime integration dependencies before final acceptance.

Documentation: update the relevant original architecture/design documents plus the generated allocation record when dependencies, estimates or acceptance evidence change. Use `dev-a/issue-136-short-description`, an up-to-date main, scoped PR, relevant tests and CI. No feature implementation is included in this allocation run.

pull_requests.body:
Closes #22 (once CI proves the database tests).
